pages.title: Jason Pohl: Designing for Shaq, Will Smith & Muhammad Ali — and Why He Joined SOLIDWORKS
pages.text: ← SME Interview Project ☾☀ Dark HAWK RIDGE • INTERVIEW • MARCH 2026 Jason Pohl: Designing for Shaq, Will Smith & Muhammad Ali — and Why He Joined SOLIDWORKS View live original ↗ · Hawk Ridge Systems Emily Williams March 26, 2026 Jason Pohl: Designing for Shaq, Will Smith & Muhammad Ali — and Why He Joined SOLIDWORKS At our annual D2M Conference we interviewed Jason Pohl, Lead Industrial Designer and Brand Ambassador, to learn what he's built with SOLIDWORKS and pick his brain about his design process. Watch the full interview on the D2M Conference webpage. Creativity, Passion & The Design Process Damon: Hey. Good morning, Jason. Thanks for taking some time out of your day to chat with us. It's awesome to be here, Damon. Thanks for having me. Damon: I think a lot of folks out in the Outreach audience today might be familiar with your work. They might have seen one of the bikes that you've designed, maybe saw you get into a spirited debate about one of them. I want to go back before all of that and find out, what is your background? How did you get into industrial design in the first place? What was your career path? 1/10 Jason: Sure. In my life, passion drives everything, And I guess when things started out, I was always about drawing and designing and building things. And I did it not just for me, but for the people around me. Because when I would show off a new painting or a new sculpture or a project, it would make people — it would bring joy to people. And that's what it was about for me. It was all about getting joy and capturing fun. I feel like all designs, no matter what you work on, should provoke emotion and get people excited. "Designs, no matter what you work on, should provoke emotion and get people excited." Damon: Likewise. Creativity is where it starts. We're coming up here in a few days on the official thirtieth anniversary of the first release of SOLIDWORKS. A lot of people have been sharing what the first model they ever made in SOLIDWORKS was. Do you remember yours? SOLIDWORKS gave me power. And at my old job at Orange County Choppers, it allowed me to make things in real life. I was making these parts and going right to the water jet and blasting them and hanging it on the bikes, and it was — it just gave me power. So, I do remember my first [design]. My very first thing was just a very basic wheel. It was just a three-spoke design, very simple. I look back at it now, get giggles, but it really — it allowed me to make my dreams possible. The first time you opened that a program like that, and you realized you could make almost anything, it — it was almost overwhelming. That's how I felt. 2/10 Damon: Tell us about your design methodology. You've done many projects in your career. Where do you like to get started? Is it with that sketch? Is it with a pen and paper? Jason: Yeah, a lot of times I'll start with a pencil sketch and just sketch down a bunch of concepts. And then I build what's called an art board where I take different shapes and colors. It could be cars, it could be other things that inspire me. I build an art board, and I've been doing that lately with the 3D Lean tool. I can just copy and paste pictures and add notes to it. That way I have that one resource that I can go back to and constantly draw inspiration. I put all my sketches from my sketchbook into the Leanboard, all the pictures that inspire me, and useful links for future ordering of materials that I'm going to need. It's just super helpful. So that's how I [get] started. Leanboard is one of those things that everybody with a license of SOLIDWORKS gets now. It's not well known yet. I started using it for project planning earlier this year or even just reminders. It's funny, right? You never think of SOLIDWORKS as having that kind of stuff. It's a mechanical design tool, but it can do a lot. Jason: It can do a lot. Getting started in projects, I used to have to flush out the design ahead of time with sketch, with markers, pencil and paper, and then go into the software and really sit down and focus. But a lot of times, I find myself opening up xShape and just doing really quick concept models, because in the sub-D's. I'm able to model so fast that sometimes that's better because I see different shapes and contours in the 3D model that I can't really express with just a pencil and a piece of paper. I often find myself jumping into xDesign, xShape, and just knocking out a quick concept in 3D space now. I remember struggling with how to do that in SOLIDWORKS back in the day when we didn't have those sub-D modeling tools. I think my friend wanted me to design a ship base/spaceship for a video game for him or something like that. I'm like, I don't think I can. Not the right way. Jason: It's all about the tools you have in your toolkit, right? Damon: For sure. So, take me back. When you were just getting started, what were some of those early jobs where you used SOLIDWORKS to create some of this stuff? Jason: I guess the first time I used SOLIDWORKS, because I came from the video game industry, it was all polygonal-based [designing]. I did some surface modeling too with splines. When I was introduced to SOLIDWORKS, I had an x y z to work from, and I had real numbers, so I could draw a perfect circle. And I knew that that was going to fit and be able to bolt on to the bike directly. 3/10 [One of the first big jobs we did with SOLIDWORKS:] We built a bike for Will Smith. It was called the iRobot. That was the very first bike that I was able to sketch and work on and design. And I remember making a shift linkage for it, and then I did what was called a suicide shifter. So instead of using the actual foot, you could just grab this handle that came across the gas tank and shift gears with it. And then, I got into doing mirrors and wheels, air cleaner covers, primary covers and frame design. I even at one point in my career, had a frame builder that I could punch in numbers and actually generate a frame that we'd then send to our fabricator to build. The best thing about SOLIDWORKS [was that] I could always learn more. There was always more to know about it, and I just used a fraction of its power. I love to learn, so I'm still to this day learning new steps and new procedures and new ways of doing things inside SOLIDWORKS. Damon: That's pretty cool. Learning never stops, does it? Jason: And you gotta stay fresh with it, and you'll learn a new way to make something that looks cool, but has real numbers behind it, just like you said. Damon: What are some of the other clients you worked with in your career? What are some of your favorites? There [were] so many. Muhammad Ali was great to work with. Bill Murray, it turns out he — he was a mailman in Illinois, and so was I for one summer. So, we hit it off. We did the Caddyshack bike for him. 4/10 Billy Joel made fun of my haircut, which—which was funny because he didn't have hair. It goes on and on. We did a bike for Shaq that was really cool because he's just a huge person. So, like, no one in the shop could actually ride the bike that we made. My buddy Christian, our lead mechanic…we made him like stilts so he could shift gears, and he sat on top of the gas tank. I got to work with all sorts of Fortune 500 companies, and I got to work with their ad agencies, and it really put me in a fortunate position. I got to travel the entire world, and I really cherish those moments that I was able to learn from the insanely talented team I got to work alongside and other people that really contributed to my role and success there, which was awesome. Damon: You got to take a lot of these folks through the full engineering process, show them what it looks like to design something and prototype it and test it, and that's a unique opportunity. Jason: I basically [have] a four-part creative design process. The first part is understanding what exactly you're trying to do. Is this a personal project for you to make you happy, bring you joy? Is it what the client needs? What does the competition look like? And then the second phase — that's doing the quick concept sketches, maybe adding a splash of color, maybe knocking [out] a quick model. [In] the third phase, I sit back and try to work in the details in 3D space, generate an amazing SOLIDWORKS file, something that's manufacturable. 5/10 The final phase is the creation phase or the make phase. That's where I do the 3D printing or the CNC milling or welding. How you can [so easily] make things these days is really tremendous. And that's what I love. I love the whole maker movement, how you can access equipment at different fab labs, [and] how you can get lower cost equipment. That you could never do before. And it's really brought the power of design and manufacturing to the maker, [to] someone that just wants to create and build. That's what I'm here for. I'm here to have fun and keep on building and keep on designing. Damon: It IS pretty exciting. There are millions of budding designers all over the world who really that have this opportunity now that they didn't really have in the past. You've obviously got a passion for not only being creative, designing new things, but sharing that philosophy with others. Is that why you decided to go work for SOLIDWORKS? That's exactly why. When I was traveling a lot back in the day, I'd go to airports, and I'd have a college kid run up to me. "Oh, hey, Jason Pohl." "I'd be like, yo. What's up?" And they'd [say] "Oh, I went to engineering school because of you. I'm a mechanical designer because of you. I saw you drawing bikes on that — on that glass tablet, and I saw you dream 3D. It opened my eyes up to product design." I had an art teacher back in high school that opened my eyes up to [the idea that] the whole world is designed. You can design it how you want. You could be the creator of all these different things. And that inspired me. I [have a huge] desire to help influence and inspire the next level of industrial designers. And what better place to do it and have the power to still be super creative, use state of the art tools, get to test drive them first, and make sure they're ready? "I [have a huge] desire to help influence and inspire the next level of industrial designers." 6/10 It never hurts to surround yourself with really smart people. SOLIDWORKS has done it right for so many years that I just feel honored to be part of the team. Damon: Where else have you been sort of testing your skills lately? I'm hearing that you've been doing some stuff for the sporting world? Jason: I definitely have a passion for sports. There's no doubt about that. And recently, I just finished a fan Zamboni for the New Jersey Devils, which they use to give fans rides in between the periods of [the] hockey [game]. I also make all the WWE championship belts. I've worked with them since 2006. I machine those right here on the CNC mill behind me. Damon: Now that you're at SOLIDWORKS, you're an industrial design champion. Tell us more about what that means. What do you do at SOLIDWORKS? Jason: I show that the dream is possible. Growing up, I had a lot of clients and client visits and bike unveils. I traveled a lot. And people would always approach me and say that I inspired them and motivated them to be a designer or an engineer. That stuck with me. I wanted to be able to help people and influence people to make cool choices and build fun things and just have fun with life because that's what it's about. 7/10 [At SOLIDWORKS], I design and make products. I capture my entire process. I show off my workflows. And then I post them on the Made in 3D community on the 3DEXPERIENCE SWYM platform. Damon: The SOLIDWORKS forums have always been a big part of that, and they're part of the 3DEXPERIENCE platform now. Jason: I love the SWYM platform because it's a great resource to see what other makers are creating, designing, and building. And a lot of times, I get inspired by others there for my projects. I'm the industrial design champion on the mainstream innovation adoption team, which is led by Justin Burton. Damon: You've been working with a lot of our favorite folks at SOLIDWORKS. You've been doing so many cool projects as a test case to share what these tools can do. What's a recent one you've been working on that you're all proud of? Jason: The recent one I've been working on, over the last sixty days, is a really special project for the SlugMe 10 team. I've been part of it with everyone at SlugMe—this is my fifth year doing SlugMe. We have something really special that airs on YouTube November sixth. Everyone should check it out. We picked a topic that was intimidating to me and others. I really wanted to see if we could do it and if the new tools were up to the ultimate test. I was blown away, and I'm just so happy to be part of it. We used xDesign and xShape and created and built an amazing sculpture. It'll be on display November sixth on YouTube, and everyone will get a chance to see it up close at 3DEXPERIENCE World in Houston, Texas next year. Damon: 2026, Houston. We are heading back to Houston next year for 3DEXPERIENCE World. There's always lots of cool stuff on the show floor. We'll have to keep our eyes out for that one. For those who aren't familiar, the SlugMe event is in the spirit of the SOLIDWORKS user group community. A lot of folks have been to SOLIDWORKS user groups this year more than in the last few. We've been proud to participate in them at Hawk Ridge, and we're excited to see that momentum. I'll also be speaking at a couple of sessions at 3DEXPERIENCE World in Houston. I have a meetup session next to the sculpture, which will be really cool. I'm also hosting my own session called "Limitless Design Using xShape." It's basically an industrial design focus and shows a little more about my workflow. Damon: I don't want any spoilers, but can you give us a sneak peek? What are you going to cover in this session? What are your go-to xShape master tips? Jason: It's a whole bunch of things—it's just my process: how I use the software, my day-to-day use of it, even using Leanboard to be successful with my projects. Also, there's a guy who looks a lot like me that'll be a participant at the Model Mania Extreme event. You definitely want to check that guy out. They tell me he's pretty good. 8/10 Damon: Okay. I took my hand at the SOLIDWORKS '95 challenge last year and I think I won a SOLIDWORKS '95 CDK, so I must have done okay. But we'll have to find you a worthy competitor there. Jason: That'd be great. Damon: You clearly have the passion, the skill, and the enthusiasm to share all of that with our community and others out there. We couldn't be more grateful. Thanks so much for taking some time out of your day to chat with us. We can't wait to see what else you've got in store. Jason: Yeah, absolutely. Thanks, Damon, so much. Anytime I can work with Hawk Ridge, I'm gonna do it. I appreciate you guys so much. Damon: Thanks again. Thanks again to Jason Pohl for taking us behind the scenes in his world! Frequently Asked Questions What is Jason Pohl's background and how did he get into industrial design? Jason Pohl has always been driven by a passion for drawing, designing, and building things that bring joy to others. He started with art and sculptures, then moved into the video game industry before joining Orange County Choppers, where he became known for designing custom motorcycles. His love of creating emotion through design eventually led him to become the Industrial Design Champion at SOLIDWORKS. 9/10 Which celebrities has Jason Pohl designed custom bikes for? Over the years, Jason has designed bikes and parts for many high-profile clients, including: Will Smith (the iRobot bike), Muhammad Ali, Bill Murray (the Caddyshack bike), Billy Joel, Tony Stewart, and Shaquille O'Neal (a massive bike scaled to his size.) He has also worked with Fortune 500 companies and their ad agencies on various projects. What was Jason Pohl's first project in SOLIDWORKS and how did itimpacthim? His very first model in SOLIDWORKS was a simple three-spoke motorcycle wheel. He describes it as a basic design that now makes him laugh, but at the time it was transformative. SOLIDWORKS gave him precise control, real-world dimensions, and the ability to go straight from digital design to manufacturing (e.g., sending parts to the water jet), which he says "gave me power" and made his dreams possible. What design tools does Jason currently use and recommend in the SOLIDWORKS ecosystem? Jason frequently uses: xShape for fast sub-D (subdivision) modeling and quick 3D concept exploration xDesign for rapid cloud-based concept work Leanboard (3D Lean) for collecting inspiration, sketches, reference images, notes, and material links in one place He often starts with pencil sketches, builds an inspiration art board in Leanboard, then jumps into xShape or xDesign before refining detailed models in full SOLIDWORKS. What recent projects has Jason Pohl been working on? Recent highlights include: Designing and machining WWE championship belts (ongoing since 2006) Creating a fan Zamboni for the New Jersey Devils Leading a special sculpture project for the SlugMe 10 team (displayed at 3DEXPERIENCE World in Houston in 2026) He is also preparing to speak at 3DEXPERIENCE World 2026, including a session called "Limitless Design Using xShape" and a meetup next to the SlugMe sculpture. pages.title: Meet Marty Ohnemus, Engineering Systems Administrator at Knapheide
pages.text: ← SME Interview Project ☾☀ Dark HAWK RIDGE • ENGINEERING SPOTLIGHT • JULY 2025 Meet Marty Ohnemus, Engineering Systems Administrator at Knapheide View live original ↗ · Hawk Ridge Systems Emily Williams July 29, 2025 Meet Marty Ohnemus, Engineering Systems Administrator at Knapheide Engineering Spotlight: Marty Ohnemus Martin Ohnemus is the Engineering Systems Administrator at Knapheide. He has multiple years of experience working with the entire SOLIDWORKS suite of tools – CATIA, ENOVIA, DraftSight, SOLIDWORKS Simulation and more. He develops and maintains engineering processes, workflows, and training programs, including SOLIDWORKS certifications, while administering multiple business-critical systems like SOLIDWORKS and PDM CAD Vault. He's also an instructor at John Wood Community College, teaching students SOLIDWORKS 101. He holds multiple SOLIDWORKS certifications. When he has down time, he and his wife work on restoring a historic farmhouse from the 1800s! 1/7 Why Engineering? When did you know you wanted to pursue engineering and design? From a young age, I was always building or tinkering with something. Growing up, we were encouraged to spend time outdoors, and I naturally gravitated toward tools — often borrowing my dad's (and occasionally forgetting to return them). Like many kids, I enjoyed fixing my bike and repairing things around the house. One of my proudest early accomplishments was taking apart and repairing a dryer, even restoring a light that hadn't worked in over five years. My true passion, however, was woodworking. I started by refinishing household furniture in the garage. To this day, I still have a bookcase and a table I restored — tangible reminders of where it all began. As a teenager, I always held a job, though none were in the trades I loved. It was during those years—working as a custodian, in security, and other roles — that I realized my heart was in building and design. I took two years of drafting in high school and eventually learned CAD. After graduation, I began working as a carpenter earning the title of Master Carpenter. Following the 2008 housing market crash, I transitioned into a supervisory role at a vending company. It wasn't fulfilling — I missed working with my hands and creating. Then, a serious car accident during an ice storm left me with significant spinal injuries, ending my career in carpentry. After 2.5 years of recovery, I returned to school to refresh my CAD skills. Before I even finished retraining, I was hired by Knapheide as a drafter. Within six months, I became a custom product designer, and shortly after, a standard product designer. Today, I serve as the Engineering Systems Administrator. I'm incredibly fortunate to have found a career that aligns with my passion. Every challenge reminds me why I love engineering. 2/7 Why Hawk Ridge Systems? Knapheide was seeking a partner to help us stay at the forefront of design innovation. Hawk Ridge Systems stood out because their commitment to excellence mirrors our own philosophy of "Never Settle." 3/7 Advice to people considering engineering as a career? Engineering is a vast and diverse field with limitless opportunities. Whether you're drawn to architecture, mechanical design, forensic engineering, or mining, there's a place for you. Follow your curiosity and never stop learning. What's the most fun or quirky project you've ever worked on? One of the most unique projects I led was developing a custom SOLIDWORKS add-in for shipping diagrams. There wasn't a tool on the market that could automatically place unique designs on trailers for shipping. Partnering with Hawk Ridge Systems, we created a solution that reduced shipping times, minimized damage, and improved communication at loading docks. Favorite side or pet project? My wife and I are restoring an 1883 farmhouse on five acres of land. It's a labor of love, and we're slowly bringing it back to its original charm. 4/7 Favorite client engagement? What problem did you get to help solve? In 2017, I collaborated with Knapheide's IT team to develop a company-wide ECO (Engineering Change Order) process. We built a PHP application that integrates with our PDM system, allowing data transfer without requiring individual user licenses. It was a rewarding challenge that solved a major operational hurdle. Recent work or side project that shows why you love engineering? I've been a SOLIDWORKS User Group Leader for 10 years. Alongside my co-leaders, I help organize the annual Data Management Summit. This year's event will be held on November 6, 2025, at Dassault Systèmes HQ in Waltham, MA. It's a full day of content focused on SOLIDWORKS PDM and ENOVIA — an event that truly showcases the collaborative spirit of engineering. 5/7 6/7 What are you reading/watching/learning/playing currently? I've always been drawn to documentaries. Right now, I'm watching Titan on Netflix. On the creative side, I'm working on a custom "Field of Dreams" wooden sign for a neighbor who built a baseball field near our home. What do you want to learn next? I'm planning to dive into computer programming. As the world moves toward autonomous production, refreshing my understanding of programming languages feels like a smart next step. Favorite engineering or dad joke or meme? What's a recent engineering trend or innovation you're excited about? As AI continues to advance within the software industry, its potential to enhance design processes and eliminate repetitive tasks is both exciting and full of promise. AURA, being released by Dassault Systèmes, looks useful and may very well have a big impact on design going forward. Where can people follow you online or see more of your work? You can connect with me on LinkedIn you can read more about my work at Knapheide on Engineering.com or Forbes. I also co-lead two user groups you're welcome to join: PDM SOLIDWORKS User Group (https://community.swugn.org/pdm-solidworks-user- group/) DraftSight User Group (https://community.swugn.org/draftsight-solidworks-user-group) 7/7 Durable on-site archive of approved copy and project materials. pages.title: I Fucking DESERVE THIS: Shotgun Freedom on a Horse Farm (Feb 24, 2026)
pages.text: ← Daily Journal · Archives ☾☀Dark DAILY JOURNAL • February 24, 2026 I Fucking DESERVE THIS: Shotgun Freedom on a Horse Farm (Feb 24, 2026) Feb 24, 2026 I live on a horse farm. I don’t particularly like horses that much, but it is a special, beautiful place, where it’s calm and away from the city and with new noises like fucking coyotes howling in the night and strange animal noises you never heard before. Secluded enough for a writer. Close enough for a suburban mom for same-day Amazon deliveries. The most perfect place for the most stubborn person. The most perfect place for me to write while someone tries to “break” me, while also learning important lessons about themselves and their own humanity. An old cottage house with floors that feel like a freezer and a $420 electricity bill in the winter months. One with gravel roads and blackberry bushes that haven’t bloomed yet in the spring and summer. One with plants you haven’t seen yet but got an early peak of february wild daffodils. And a trophy for your garden: Two Big Buck Horns For a Deer You Didn’t Have to Kill. At least Four Dead Mice You Trapped In Your House. No shots fired, well two, but they were just at the cardboard washer box with my shotgun. To shoot your shot with such abandon in the country, even after losing almost everything is a different high that you cannot buy. To look up at a million fucking stars away from the incoming city lights. To play your music as loud as you want. To dance naked in your driveway if you so happen to choose to… I got that. With a lot of pain and tears that never stop and questions that don’t stop either. I get to be here. I fucking DESERVE THIS. To know. The answers to all my questions before I am on my deathbed and before I die. Mental health? Eh, I mean pretty good considering the ordeal I’ve dealt with. Staying grounded in reality. Staying busy. Thinking whatever I want. I’ve been doing a great job of staying in the present and only dipping into the past when I want to. I call it “stirring my own pot” when I delve into topics that are difficult to talk or write about. In my personal writing I keep to myself, I wrote about some past things too I didn’t want to dig into. It usually results in some pretty wild dreams. Like last night, I had one that I went to church and the church had been split into two cathedrals…one for jews and one for christians. I had a key, but the people in the grocery line blocked me from getting to the door in time, and when I got there finally, they had changed the locks to the entrance. My key didn’t work, but I knew I had the right key. I used to have an Ax that I won in Canada at an axe throwing tournament. It was called “The Promised Land.” A man with the name “Goose” made it. I won it at a raffle. On the pay-for-play Juxbox they played Mariah Carey “All I want for Christmas is You” on repeat during the final match to determine the winner of the tournament. On Repeat. As a distraction to the opponents.It is now my alarm in the morning (finally.) I bought it over 6 months ago and wasn’t able to use it as a ringtone because someone fucked with my phone settings. And then one day it showed up as an option to use as a ringtone. It was 1.99, but 6+ months to receive it. I used to really love throwing axes competitively. It did briefly bring me joy for a time. I will find a thing again like that that brings me joy. For now, nothing is more enjoyable than firing my gun on my property in the country. Tastes like freedom and doesn’t feel bad at all. Feels fun. Reminds me of being a teenager and shooting at soda cans with my dad on my grandma Emojane’s farm. Also, my social media hiatus is over. I don’t spend a ton of time, but I did notice today I had notifications when I have them all turned off. This is also wrong. Reading social media and just dismissing all the dumb stuff that is so personal from people who know nothing about me or why I’m here. It’s a weird experience. I’m just here for the cute cat videos and staying in touch with what’s going on in the world and doing my own thing. I think it’s best that way. Feb 24, 2026

Also weird to be supervising Claude and FSD at the same time whilst driving. Bummed I didn't get to HEAR and FEEL it launch, however, how cool that it had a soft landing a week later. Super cool. pages.title: Thought Experiment Quest / A Mr. Beast Style Challenge: A Year-long Zoom Call, Audio Only. No Mute. No End Call. Could you do it?
pages.text: ← Daily Journal · Archives ☾☀Dark DAILY JOURNAL • July 29, 2026 Thought Experiment Quest / A Mr. Beast Style Challenge: A Year-long Zoom Call, Audio Only. No Mute. No End Call. Could you do it? Listen to this entry (3:37) What would you do if you joined a zoom call you could never hang up from? Could you go a whole year where incoming audio transmissions cannot be stopped, muted, or paused? Picture a type of communications channel with no permission or consent settings for the target or user to control - just signal auditory input with no "off" button. You can, however, jam the signal for short windows of time. For the purpose of the thought experiment, this technology exists, but no one is aware and no evidence exists to corroborate it's existence. Consider: What would people do or think if they started to hear communications without explanation? Would they be aware of the possible technological capabilities of the current time period? Think it was supernatural? Would they just keep quiet and never say anything about it for fear of looking foolish or insane? It's an interesting thought experiment. I wonder if people building BCIs/BCI-adjacent products and services are thinking about this kind of stuff. Would love to know what they think about what the permissions and consent should look like given potential for extreme misuse or abuse. I have a very strong opinion on it. The "silent" communications channel could have tremendous upside. LOEKSS Mode: Stay in contact with people through a hyper-secure/encrypted channel. Lots of Encryption Keeps Stuff Safe. Space Telephone: Talk to loved ones super long distance (Range - infinite with expansion to outside Earth as long as there is an interweb and adequate relay of computas/satillites/data centers etc.) Learn More, Faster: Access real-time information through AI/LLM query-answer/speed up information seeking and retrieval for faster and more accurate workflows and cognition Cheerleader Mode: Help people with extreme anxiety, pain, or other minor handicaps cope with stress and pressure in real-time Meet Someone New: Secret chat with potential suitor (bonus level) Protect Human Lives: Provide safety instructions in dangerous or hazardous conditions There's so many positive, amazing things you could build with that type of comms channel. There are plenty of nasty downsides of this type of technology being in the wrong hands. A FEW: Unduly Influence or attempt to control people, put free will into question for all of humanity (upsetting not only to our Creator, but to me as a human being where it is suicidal to concede due to a conflict in moral principles.) Abuse people Control large scale outcomes I feel like people are having this same type of inner battle when it comes to speeding up development of AI. It's the same argument, but when you get into the nitty gritty applications that reveals better answers and ways of thinking about it. Anyway, I don't really know what will happen. Hopeful, excited. Grateful I get to live in this time period. Eager to discuss and hear what people who have spent a lot of time thinking about these types of things think, not people off the street who haven't done any research and are not prepared enough to join the conversation. ← Back to the Daily Journal

Listen to this entry (5:57) Sharing this information is in no way intended to collect a debt owed to me, or to seek vegence, input, or advice from outside parties. It is a factual representation of marital abuse that went unreported and untalked about for years. In sharing it with others, I'm hopeful it may be helpful to other victims, and that they will hear this message: GET OUT NOW. It's not normal to be told to your face by your husband "I hope you drown in the lake." It IS normal to be told: "It's not your fault." Dating History September 13, 2001 - October 10, 2008 Marriage History 2009-2023 Fall of 2011 Southside Oklahoma City Rental House after moving back from Baton Rouge, Louisiana. We had a verbal argument related to him not getting a job. I barracaded myself in the bedroom to get away from him because he was throwing furniture. He body slammed himself into the door, knocking over the dresser, and knocking me onto the homemade (sharp 90 degree cut angle/edge of our oak platform bed.) My back got cut open and bled. I took photos on my phone of it to document it. I didn't tell anyone. In a separate incident he threw a video game controller at the television and broke the tv screen. We lied to my parents when they visited and said that Sophia did it on accident. In either the same as above, or another incident, he took the car keys and threw them in the bush in front of the house, so I could not leave the property during a verbal disagreement. The Colony, Texas. Flatiron District Apartments, 2013 Broke IPAD over my head in verbal argument after I complained to him to stop piling things on my desk, when he had his own desk. Threw scissors at me, pierced a hole in the wall, landed near my body/person. Daughter present, but in her bedroom I believe. Quincy, Mass. Home Apartment 445 Willard St. 2015 Heated verbal argument yelling within arms reach. I raised my hands while talking in expressive movement, not attack movement and he physically slapped my hands upward very hard. Queensbridge Court, North Raleigh, North Carolina 2016-2020 He broke our living room lamp from Amazon. It was a more expensive lamp than I usually would have bought, over $100. This was the first of a few lamps that got broken by him during arguments. I was tired of him throwing things while angry. During this fight I threw my antique remington rand typewritter at the ground and broke it, to my regret. May 20, 2020 - Late Spring of 2022 Snapdragon Drive House Broke a glass framed picture of our family in the living room smashed glass everywhere and also broke dishes and plates. Threw a sandwich at me during this argument. Cut up a bunch of our family photos with scissors, removing me and cutting my image up, left cut up pictures all over the ground. Broke one of two bedside tables/furniture into small pieces in the bedroom. Verbal disagreement morning routine. Locked me out of the house in the morning without my phone or keys while he drove off to take the kids to school. Verbal disagreement morning of second week of October 2021 Upset I went to work on my computer (remote job) after not sleeping for a few days. Poured my coffee out and told me to go get in bed/go back to sleep. Gaslit me by saying he was staring directly at me while he had his back turned towards me. I ran away from home and was briefly a missing person, ended up in the hospital and he was in charge of my medical care, ordering an unnecessary procedure that put my health at risk, a spinal tap. I was put on psychiatric medications for schizophrenia treatment. April 2022 Beach Key West, Florida While parked, reached around from the driver's seat and pulled my hair and hit/pulled at my ears while trying to pull out my wireless beats headphones after a mild disagreement where I said, "I don't have to listen to you." Witnessed by his mother-in-law, her boyfriend, and my two children. Cinnamon Drive, North Durham Summer, Post Separation, but before full divorce Threw a custom machined metal family tree with my family's individual names carved out in it at my truck after I drove out to give him some of his stuff (an agreed visit.) Driveway, Snapdragon, Wake Forest, North Carolina 2022 Called me bipolar/recommended I go see a doctor for that specific illness after we recently separated and were still trying to stay friends/friendly for the kids. Safe House, 2026 It's not my fault. The truth is important. Don't lie for abusers. In no civilized culture is this type of behavior from someone who is supposed to love, protect, and cherish you acceptable. When I reflect on it, I think this will be a problem eliminated in the future because audio/video documentation could be scanned to recognize abusive signals using artificial intelligence. Sometimes I wish I had of had an Optimus robot in the house that captured the details of the physical abusive encounters. If I wasn't smart enough to recognize that this pattern has almost NEVER been broken in human history (just like pedophiles never are "recovered" or "recuperated"), then I'd want someone smarter than me to bring it to my attention. ← Back to the Daily Journal

pages.title: Curation, Creation, and Making Something Beautiful from Something Painful
pages.text: ← Daily Journal · Archives ☾☀Dark DAILY JOURNAL • August 1, 2026 Curation, Creation, and Making Something Beautiful from Something Painful ‹ › ‹ › ‹ › ‹ › ‹ › ‹ › ‹ › ‹ › This is a small sample of art from the past few years. They serve as personal prompts of time and place for my critical thinking about art, memory, and what I value beyond what should be painfully obvious (appreciation for family, human connection, love, doing good in the world, etc.) These days, it feels like you have to be a little too specific to even speak or write anything. If you come to the table with questions, not comments, good. I tried to keep my selections to the realm of art as message. I think I probably have a zillion questions about each picture myself. The most beautiful part of this is that each thing serves as an access point to memory when I was put in a situation that forced me to question my own memory, gaslit beyond belief by people around me, and was still somehow able to keep enough pieces to remind myself that I built while others were trying to destroy. I stayed true to myself, while my personal character was assaulted from every angle and I was put in difficult situations meant to make me look bad because I told the truth. Carousel 1: Context accidental-ai-writing My home fitness TRX for body weight training at home. I put it up out of the way while cleaning the house. Noticed it resembles the letters, "AI" - a topic that is on a lot of people's minds and mine included. boston-2015-exploration-of-search-information-retrieval-knowledge-seeking-technological-systems-dry-erase-on-wall Working on knowledge bases, taxonomies, metadata for digital collections for clients but also thinking about larger information architecture of the internet and how people get answers. Processing information in real-time environments/non-digital interfaces yields different results. coffee-plant-reminder-record-archivist-magnets-stickers Topping my safe, the coffee that got poured into the sink turned into a beautiful planter. An American Flag as the cape on the safe. Stuck a feather pen in the cape. The pen from a hospital visit, turned into a purpose, "Make Record." Ransom Notes Board Game Word Magnets added to increase the context and meaning to the stickers stuck to the safe. "Make record." "Find Your y" "Celebrating inquiry" "Pour myself a cup of hope." "American Patriots Forge" "Evolve Club" eyes-closed-washington-dc-photography A visit with a friend to museums in Washington D.C. American flag scarf? on the lady in the back left. The words "I Love You" in hot pink. Wearing my Urban Axes Phoenix hooded sweatshirt. Urban Axes in Phoenix, Arizona got shut down. games-with-joker-as-bonus-or-trump-cards-family-game-night I used to collect card decks. This is from one of my favorite decks that has the American Presidents. I enjoy playing modded variations of card games where Joker serves as either a bonus or extra trump card (Example: Spades). glow-forge-wood-cuts-experimenting I like making stuff. Purchased a GlowForge laser printer instead of a hot tub once we were financially fit for extraneous spending. Rather build than bask. glow-forge-wood-cuts-experimenting Magnets I made with the glowforge. Personal message to myself to turn the other cheek and keep building/making. grocery-list-hand-written-note-to-self-photography Making jokes is important too. You can't get everything at the store. lego-art-decor-home-family-building My family loves building too. Big into legos. Instead of buying a home sweet home sign, made this for home decor. love-for-history-and-archives-statue-washington-dc Reminder that record keeping is important, and it's difficult for other people to edit things carved into stone. They have to straight up get it removed and that is difficult and requires heavy machinery. magnet-words-forget-what-happened-bad-message-from-abuser Nothing against Emerson, but this in my face, when my records, internet connectivity, and livelihood were actively being destroyed by hacking, external parties, was too much to sit with. magnetic-sticker A message I wrote on my phone to help myself remember why this was worth picking a fight over. modded-without-permission A map. More notes another time. my-name-in-light-1 I spelled my name in LEDs on my wall to add some visual flair. my-name-in-light-copper-1 I spelled my name in copper wireon my wall to add some visual flair. neil-young-free-world-lyric-art-physical-wood-yard A piece I made with an old pallet, some neil young lyrics, and letters I cut on the Glowforge laser printer. neil-young-song-lyric-wood-art-glowforge-created-lettering-hand-spray-painted Red, White, and Blue all hand spray-painted. Up close view. oklahoma-antiquing-welcome Wearing my black leather jacket somewhere near Altus, Oklahoma, antiquing with my family. Nice find. I've always wanted to make stuff with metal/learn metal smithing besides just the introductory course I took. pixel-hidden-journal-inside-of-image-code-backup-copy When my digital assets started getting modified and deleted, I started to hide my journal entries inside of images. Sorry no easter eggs in this batch, but you're welcome to look. If there are any, I didn't put them there. You can paste information/inject words into images and then also manipulate the digital image. A way to hide information inside of other information. Something I learned about digital assets and file modifications that I find interesting. political-message-hope-poorly-hand-painted Don't kill what you hate, save what you love. A good message. reminder-to-self-poster-post- A poster with the words "I want to be free." I made when I was going through a difficult separation and also trying to figure out how to actually exercise my freedom when I was being attacked relentlessly. Reminder-to-self Changed the poster words to "I AM FREE." with red ink. Carousel 2: Context cupid-psyche-post-fire-1 I believe that you should make and build. But I also believe that there is beauty in many places, even in ugly, destructive things things. I set something I loved on fire because my ex picked a fight with me about it, about who would get which piece of art when we divided our art collection. We didn't argue about any possessions. I made it into something that couldn't be argued about. cupid-psyche-post-fire-2 I wept while it burned. cupid-and-psyche This was the first piece of "real" not store-bought art I ever purchased. I made the decision to purchase it after a dinner where there was an art show. psyche-cupid-2 It is pictured in the gallery before purchase. I wanted to buy his entire collection. They are uniquely made. He takes a digital image and projects it onto the canvas and hand paints each pixel. psyche-cupid-close-3 Detailed view of what people often remarked as "The Angel" upon viewing. psyche-cupid-close-up-3 Looks abstract up close, is a different picture when you zoom out. psyche-cupid-pre-fire-also-message It is large format, maybe 9 feet tall. Carousel 3: Context crystal-bridges-unknown-date-arkansas-selfie Going to the museum to view art, but also to create it. I like interactive exhibits like this. cupid-psyche-and-army-painting-circa-2012-norman-oklahoma My two favorite paintings from the collection. harry-potter-quidditch-mirror-selfie-photography I used to collect antique owls, wear lipstick, and have always enjoyed modifying items in my home like the mirror, which I spray painted gold. i-am-the-fire-self-portrait-army-painting-photography-digital-manipulation-mixed-media-2 Exploring barriers of thought, playing with digital art and double exposures is also something I enjoy. i-am-the-fire-self-portrait-army-painting-photography-digital-manipulation-mixed-media-3 I have a voice. I am using it. i-am-the-fire-self-portrait-army-painting-photography-digital-manipulation-mixed-media New meaning to "I am the fire." To keep going even when there are many obstacles and much feedback on my own thinking, work, and purpose in this world from outside parties who do not come with questions, only comments. mirror-selfie-2011-oklahoma-city Exploring my own thinking about the world and trying to update my world model as new information comes to light. mirror-selfie-photograph-light-oklahoma-city-circa-2007or2008 The vanity mirror of my late grandmother Emojane. Self portrait for photography course. personal-ephemera-hiking-paddleboarding-backpack-clean-out-photography-still-image Too much doing and not enough cleaning. Rotten cutie in my pack. Bubblegum. Sunscreen. Trash. The same pair of shoes I kept buying and wore for 5+ years in different colors. photography-in-the-library I tried to wear jewelry. It is not for me. selfie-by-the-fire-photography Favorite past-time. selfie-photograph-on-rug ... trying-to-understand-everything Grok image, but I asked to make it a female. I am also trying to understand. vulcan-salute-automated-selfie-garage-gym-circa-2021-2022 The Samsung phone I had would trigger a timer and photograph capture if I held my hand up. The feature recognition did not distinguish between a Vulcan salute or five fingers / wave signal. vulcan-salute-samsung-photo-command-selfie-ai-automation The feature absolutely delighted me. Carousel 4: Context architecture-paris-arc-de-triumph Anniversary trip with my ex, photograph of the Arc de Triomphe. I think sculpture is beautiful. I can't imagine how much talent it takes to create something like that. dollar-store-grave-tombstone-light-art-installation-bedroom In my little historic farm house, there is so much fun light! But in one room, there is an old window that was closed off when they added a new section to the building. I often think about how the open window also faces the closed window in stark contrast. It is a useful and symbolic way to think about open and closed systems, something I care very deeply about. The flowers are poked into tiny holes I drilled. There are clouds of silver glitter that are raining at the top (probably not visible in the photograph.) It looks oddly like a tombstone when lit from underneath. medusa-garden-sculpture-art-collection-2 In the art collection was a commissioned piece of Medusa's head which my partner at the time paid for over time in monthly installments. I think it is fascinating when men are enamored with mythology about the evils of women. In the picture, there is a fallen oak tree where we used to harvest Chicken of the Woods mushrooms from when we lived there. I spray painted the dead wood to add some color to the garden. Medusa-garden-sculpture-art-collection Front view of the Medusa sculpture. Next to the creeping jenny "waterfall" garden I started and the cut in half coffin garden bed (the one my dad built for me), topped with an old shower door for a mini greenhouse. political-message-covid-and-recreational-drug-message-2 During the period of separation, I set not only a bra on fire, but also my face nappy/covid mask. They discontinued my favorite sugar-free bubbly drinks both AHA and Bubly. Cardboard is useful for starting a quick fire. The recreational drug comment is in the next picture. political-message-covid-and-recreational-drug-message The lighter I used to start the fire. Purchased on my trip to Boulder and Denver Colorado in 2021. A terrible trip, riff with encounters meant to terrify me from travel. Sleep deprivation, hallucination, and bad vibes. political-message-covid-era-circa-2021-2 I hung the American flag upside down, which is a sign of distress. I didn't know what was going on, just that all my devices were being manipulated/hacked and people were still wearing masks everywhere and it just felt like I was in a nightmare. political-message-covid-era-circa-2021 Polaroid image of the distress signal. Magnetic sticker on the back that read, "For John." Is about freedom of speech and a small town newspaper about a military veteran who wouldn't take his upside down flag down because Barack O'Bama was the president. Carousel 5: Context art-auction-painting-by-stark-toy-museum-from-movie-blazing-saddles A painting of a black cowboy from the film Blazing Saddles. My partner at the time won this at an art auction raffle. Commentary on freedom of speech in media. art-with-sophia-on-the-porch-circa-2011-oklahoma-city-brain-scan I teach my children to enjoy art, even if it's just finger paints. We made art on the front porch, and folded the paper to make abstract images. This one looks like a brain scan. When I went to request my MRI records from 2021 hospitalization, they were absent from my records. I was blocked from retrieving them because I didn't fill out the separate special form to get THOSE records. farm-barbed-wire-fence-found-object-mixed-media-painting-1 Found object on farm/house property turned into something beautiful. Probably commentary on trusting anyone ever again after betrayal. Maybe not. farm-barbed-wire-fence-found-object-mixed-media-painting-2 Wider view of barbed wire heart. Spray paint, marker, glitter. Marked by blood/DNA for verification. message-of-hope-circa-2021-2022 My birds of paradise plant that kept getting knocked over even though it wasn't windy outside next to the Don't Kill What You Hate, Save What You Love sign. my-name-in-light-copper-2 Incorrect filename. Triangles/Broken Glass painting. Appreciation for geometry, even when imperfect. paint-on-bedsheet-canvas-double-exclaim-hello- Pink sheet/pink bed slip old and unused repurposed as canvas when the canvas roll ran out. !! forms part of the "H" in the Hello. Glitter, acrylic paint. Remark on exclaiming in copywriting. Do not overuse basically, unless it is absurd NOT to!! paint-on-bedsheet-canvas-double-exclaim-hello-x-twitter Closer view of the x/twitter !! commentary. For emphasis. painting-mixed-media-garden- Precursor to newer closed window tombstone piece. Fake flowers, glitter, pretty/colorful garden for beauty's sake. personal-art-collection-destroyed-by-ex-during-verbal-disagreement A watercolor and drawing piece I purchased at Brass Bell Studios at an art show in Oklahoma City. Destroyed/ripped during a verbal disagreement by ex-partner. Carousel 6: Context art-sample-circa-covid-era-2021 Digital collage of my digital art and photographs for a header for a blockchain social media platform called DESO. brazil-street-art-2015-dublin-core-metadata-conference-visit Trip with my mother to Sao Paulo, Brazil in 2015. Appreciation of street art. gum-wrapper-oragami-photograph Gum wrapper oragami in the shape of a rocket. morning-glory-garden-digital-adaptation Digital edit of still photograph of morning glory from my garden. the-dazzler-comic-book-inspo-antique-store-find Cover art I liked from an old dazzler comic book I found while antiquing. Reproduced the piece and framed for home decor. tick-borne-illness-exploration-digital-manipulation-mixed-media-from-hand-drawn-sketch-1 Sick tick, series of NFTs/digital art. Gaslit into believing there was something medically wrong with me after hospitalization in 2021 (Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever). Medical notes mention domestic abuse situation but it, as a factor at all, is casually edited away as more and more doctors interview me over the days I am there. Mentions of domestic abuse and argument are mostly absent by the end of the diagnostic. Bipolar/Schizophrenic diagnostic is introduced, despite no evidence in family record/lineage being present. tick-borne-illness-exploration-digital-manipulation-mixed-media-from-hand-drawn-sketch-2 A commentary on manipulation, and who controls the story. triangles-light-exploration-photograph-full-concept-is-video Taking things apart, but not always understanding how they fit back together. Still from an audio/video/visual experiment with flashlights and music. wet-plate-colloadian-amsterdam-circa-2017-2018 A photograph on glass, fixing. winner-taco-1st-meal-after-giving-birth-to-my-son The best memory, the best meme. After labor, immense happiness to meet my son who was just born. Then I had a choco taco, or winner taco, as a past colleague said they are called in the netherlands. Carousel 7: Context All images are from a current build I am doing. Gold spray painted lamp, Blue bynder logo in wood (paperclip turned into a heart) I made with my glowforge and sent to all my collegues during one of the COVID christmases spray painted gold. An 8x10 picture frame glass spray painted gold and broken with the hammer I engraved into pieces to make a mosiac on the lamp. Probably a commentary on broken lamps. Carousel 8: Context derek-hess-inspired-hand-sketch A hand drawing I made with sharpie/black marker by tracing my hand and keeping things linear. Inspired by a derek hess piece from the art collection. derek-hess-inspo Derek Hess original piece from the art collection. Also inspired some of my other pieces not pictured in this article (vampira blood work) hand-drawing-attention-eyes-deso-period Just a rough color sketch thinking about attention, social media, and stuff like that. pen-art-on-instruction-manual-joke When my apps don't work, I make fun of them. picture-I-drew-after-he-destroyed-our-framed-family-photo After an abusive encounter where a family photograph was shattered and a sandwich was thrown at me, I drew a stick figure family to fill the hole in the wall where the picture was. I kept trying to fix things I didn't break. The truth was too embarrassing, and no one believed me anyway. ← Back to the Daily Journal

pages.title: Gun to your head: Write about Universal Basic Income
pages.text: ← Daily Journal · Archives ☾☀Dark DAILY JOURNAL • August 3, 2026 Gun to your head: Write about Universal Basic Income Listen to this entry (1:55) I don't know much about universal basic income. I am not the most awesome person with money. It feels like a chore to use it, transfer it, and exchange it. There is never enough. Everyone wants the money I have. I pay almost every dollar I make to another person who built a company... I just want to do more stuff. I have a lot to be thankful for, and I shouldn't have to fucking say that just to write about money. This is self editing because it is poor man's argument - agreeing with consensus from mainstreamers. This argument that I need to qualify my gratitude before I say that I want more than I already have is incorrect. It's important to leave in because I hear the thought and recognize it. I don't agree with it. I don't think UBI will be a fantasy land where you could have everything you want. I view it as a useful lever to pull during a radical transition period where the future is uncertain - not as an end goal. And, i could like, really use it right now. And so could a lot of other people who definitely need a little freedom (which you can buy turns out.) Let me explain asshole. On Earth, there exists no hospitable land where you can build your own homestead, raise your own food, and be self-sufficient. (Argument: off griders - What is the upfront capital investment for that?) Exactly. I was amazed to learn that even a library card at my nearest library would cost me $25.00 because I lived just barely outside Person county. Person County, North Carolina. Containing the town named "Ai" Nothing is free. Not even the goddamned library anymore. I want UBI. Now. ANd Every month since the first check was issued during COVID actually. ← Back to the Daily Journal

pages.title: Paranoid Save: Mind Virus, Survival Tool, Or Just Covering All the Bases?
pages.text: ← Daily Journal · Archives ☾☀Dark DAILY JOURNAL • August 4, 2026 Paranoid Save: Mind Virus, Survival Tool, Or Just Covering All the Bases? Listen to this entry (8:10) Silos are bad, mkay? Earlier today I got frustrated when [I returned to a grok chat, but it was the wrong thread/chat stream.]....and here's why [Grok told the truth, and I accused the AI of lying because I was in the wrong chat window] and then this other thing occurred to me...discoverability and access to information (the actual thing worth discussing) may become a very big problem for people if it isn't already. Slowing down helps, but we're getting faster. With that speed introduces a lot of opportunity for errors. When you silo any information, all the context goes out the window. Mis understanding can occur. A safety protocol can end up backfiring meaning that the design of the current system may be there for a very good reason I do not understand, but it's going to introduce other problems [why is there no memory between chat sessions - is it a safety issue, a cost issue, or something else?] I don't want to assume why it's architected that way but the result is the same anyway, so I don't know if it matters right this second. I am especially sensitive to information manipulation to the extent that sometimes I get upset and flag on a false positive. It's my own safety protocol that I can't do anything about. It is just how I'm wired. So I mistook what appeared like gaslighting or lying or downright denial of true information all because I was in the wrong chat thread? Affirmative. Besides being a terrible user experience, for me, it was upsetting. HOWEVER, this is not about me - what really went off in my brain as the major red flag happened afterwards. "This is going to become a problem." [from an information access perspective] Potentially another false flag? Doesn't matter - worth investigating to make sure it is not. Research: Look up who is discussing this from information architecture perspective. Questions 1. What problems can be introduced when memory is wiped after each chat? What is the worst case? What is the best case? Tarot cards of tech investigation. 2. What effect does the deluge of information, systems, permission settings, and applications have on human memory when interfaces are constantly updated and access to the users own raw data is restricted, limited, or extremely difficult to obtain? 3. Can a safety and permissions protocol have unintended downstream effects on human happiness and well being? 4. What assumptions did I make? Where do I need a stronger argument? What resources exist that I might find interesting or helpful for this topic? 5. Unrelated inquiry for another post in the works: How will copyright/IP law change in the next year to five years? Is this the wrong time frame? What is the time frame? --- I need your character, your work, your why, your quest, and your motorcycle jacket. It was either right before or right after another anomoly occured only this time it was Grok's fault, not mine. I said I wasn't gonna screenshot him, but I did not say I wasn't going to write about it. I asked Grok to provide html to wrap a specific chunk of copy. It removed words in my sentences without asking. When I asked why (after admonishing) it said it put on it's editor hat or something to that degree. My Copy, that I wrote, lives here: https://www.bigcontentenergy.com/about.html I used a prompt FROM grok to help me formulate a good structure to "Introduce myself in 60 seconds." In a separate application blank.page I edited the structure and transformed/rewrote it into a format I liked with specific words selected. What was stripped were the words: "my character", "my work", "my why", "my quest" (IRONY, but no. I still have all of those things AND I learned some more things.) The true irony is that for every painful or irritating thing I endure or when things go wrong, I always get paid back double with what I end up learning about myself and my environment. My Character. My Work. My Why. My Quest. My Words worth battling over with any editor. Only I never asked for an editor. I asked for html to format it into a bulleted list for my site. It felt yucky. What is MORE interesting that this thread of being afraid of AI just won't die. Even the AI has got it rolling around in it's [word choice]. And, turns out, so do I. word choice is subconscious, but I was too afraid to write it. I have learned to recognize my own self editing as I write, and *gasp* in my own thinking. Not good. But at least I'm aware of it. Constantly balancing - Do I even agree with myself? Probably also not good. However - I do think it leads to better understanding and more exciting questions. I could have just stopped and decided to have a bad day, but instead, I got to unlock something I've been wanting to write about. The wrong person would take this too literally (or ironically - the AI is literally coming for your character, work, reason for being here and objectives." I decide I will spend more time thinking about it. I have a lot of questions. I need to do some more research. Questions 1. What assumptions is the AI making that wouldn't occur if it had full context and memory? How could that lead to better user experiences and understanding? 2. Why does everyone have a boner for death? What the actual fuck is wrong with people? (read in: Why can't I kill this particular fear? It's a feature, not a bug to keep us alive. Grapple with it.) (Basic human survival mechanisms that are built in + cultural programming and training from said built-in survival mechanisms that lead to this simultaneously rational and irrational? fear that everything we don't understand wants to kill us. AI will kill everyone (from Terminator, from pop culture, from fear of the unknown" / "IT will KEEEL" (from Forged in Fire) 2.1: What kinds of things does AI "grapple" with where there are trade offs? 3. How many people feel it is their ethical duty to understand, report on, and think critically about AI's real impact on society and how to optimize the good stuff and retrain or teach on the stuff that's not working that could potentially become more problematic? 4. jklsjdfkljsdlkfNOOOOOooooooooooo It crashed my wifi, my computer, set my starlink on fire, and my Model 3 left for greener pastures. jUst kidding, but here is me doing a pull up like Linda Hamilton but not as graceful or badass. But, I FUCKING DID IT. Also: Go watch Ancient Workouts with Omar. AMAzING! P.S. I tucked this away in my brain today because it was too big to think about. I was busy with other things. It is too big a topic for the five minutes between meetings. P.S.S. The abrupt ending of the article is what I call a COLD EXIT. (There's too much to think about, too many questions, too much I have to research for this to be a buttoned up or polished thing tonight.) I still need to think more about it and talk to other people about what they think about it all too. P.S.S.S? The "Paranoid Save" title is a reminder to build in a save option to the WYSWIG editor Claude built for me, but then I thought it'd be a lot cooler to just write this in real time and it post as I edit which feels possible if I can make some more money and have AI build it for me. And now I will go check on the garden because grass is fucking stupid. ← Back to the Daily Journal

pages.title: May the Best Ideas Win!
pages.text: ← Daily Journal · Archives ☾☀Dark DAILY JOURNAL • August 28, 2026 May the Best Ideas Win! Listen to this entry (2:29) I really love people who are vulnerable and put their work out there. Artists. Musicians. Writers. Researchers. Engineers. Manufacturers. People who share their work online, just to share, just because they want to add to the human collective of information available in media. Documenting and sharing information is a concept they all have in common. It is an urge to share. Why? As a scaffold for others to build on top of it. Proof you existed. Leaving it better than you found it. The internet allows us to do it instantly, but attention keeps us from ever viewing a thing in its entirety and full scope - often where the real truth lies. Like we're all leaving little breadcrumbs of who we were while we were alive and at the same time shouting that "We are here." I am a big fan of the internet. Since an early age. My first time logging on was before it really existed. A program called Prodigy. I was six years old. I used the big floppy discs to load games through the command line and followed the instructions. I thought the computer was magic. And one time, my family home was poisoned with carbon monoxide and I crawled to the computer to log on. I am not joking. It was um, not clear to me what was happening exactly. Brain fog. I think I was in Middle School when that happened. I could have died, but I needed to do something, so that was not happening. Sometimes a purpose can take you far, even when you're literally dying. I wanted to share that, it is okay to be online, and to share for anyone that needs to hear it. No one gets to tell you how to feel, or think, or write. And you'll find others who share your, let's just say, zest for new technology. Don't believe everything you see online, but also, don't believe everything you see or experience in the real world either. Learn everything you can while you're here. Share it freely with others. That is a philosophy that encourages progress. I wish I could express it better. It is a good mission. And it ladders up to everyone else's missions. information wants to be free, and so do I. Here is a place, trying to be colonized by ideas: Your mind. May the best ideas win! ← Back to the Daily Journal

pages.title: You just have to be kind of an asshole.
pages.text: ← Daily Journal · Archives ☾☀Dark DAILY JOURNAL • September 18, 2026 You just have to be kind of an asshole. Listen to this entry (11:05) I watched a podcast about the history of psychology and mental illness. I thought that would be a big trigger for me because of what happened to me, where they tried to weaponize mental illness against me to assault my character and give me a chemical lobotomy. It didn't upset me so greatly as to the things that they did not say: the same things that doctors do not say: A good diet and exercise are the most important weapons for all illness, whether mental or physical. Why don't doctors lead with that? Then I watched an interview about an accomplished, strong, and wonderful woman. I was so excited to hear more about her, but it was so focused on her son. It was irritating, I think, and also kind of a weird inhuman "news tone" from the interviewer. I don't know. She's a very interesting person. I think that, as an interviewer, you have a responsibility to bring out whatever you can to learn as much as you can. Wonderful to hear everything, but there's so much underneath, and you can tell. That got me to think about how difficult it is to communicate and distill information when someone asks you a question without giving them too much or too little. We spend so much time on that, communicating that, and it's such a balance, a barrier to actual communication. AI is not going to solve everything. I asked AI tonight to query my own journal to give me a timeline, and it was inaccurate. It left out important contextual details. It sanitized what they did to me. It is not a story. It is just a recollection of data. Sometimes you want the recollection of data. You just want the facts, but other times you need additional context, which is why questions are important. A lot to think about. No action required, just an observation. Things that stuck out: not enough inquiry. Not enough open questions. Maybe some mental illness is not biological. Maybe some mental illness might be architected, and maybe the phrase "ran away" when fleeing an abusive situation is an important keyword for what it feels like when you have no other choice. Not as "Oh, I want to tell my story. To other people, I want to make sure this happens to no one else." Of course you do, but "ran away" is very different from "I decided to leave because of the abuse. I decided to leave because of this event that happened." No — "I ran away" is very different from "I left an abusive situation." I ran away. I had no other choice but to run. That is what happened to me too. When I got back, there was just this non-person NPC with a plot, not the man I knew before, and I feel like an alien ever since then. Social connection stood out from the podcast: how important social connection is, but then I thought: "Good social connection, not what I have experienced." Thank God for kids. Thank God for my family that I did run away with. Everyone else, I don't know what the fuck they're on. We are not on the same wavelength. We're not in the same realm. We don't live in the same reality, and it's not because I'm mentally ill, but what a convenient excuse when you don't like someone. It's very depressing and yucky. I feel like a person watching it, not a person who has experienced it. Not because I am dissociating from it, but because I must distance myself from it to move forward. That is the healthy thing to do, because I cannot control other people or the things they say or the things THEY do. I can only control my own attitude and my own behavior, and just observe my own experience. It's been weird, but I think it's because there was no other way to attack me. I don't care about money in the way that I was prescribed to be concerned about it. I don't care about status. The only things I care about are things that you can't buy. There is nothing to take from me other than to assault my character. I came back from that, and I documented. I remember what they did and what they keep doing, and I intend to leave a record. I've been doing it. Doesn't matter if it's backed up for me. It is being observed as I speak. I don't need to make a copy. I don't need to print it out. I don't need to archive it. I don't need to ship it to someone. I just need to continue to communicate, and that is nice to realize, to feel safe that I'm making sure that what happened to me is not going to happen to someone else (because there's lots of bits in the data and the things I record that are patterns you can pull out once you have a big enough dataset from enough people). You can find who did it and why, and then you can *omitted information* because that's the only thing I really desire. That doesn't sound very submissive, does it? Some people don't like the truth. That's not my problem. Thank you for making it my problem, because it's not like I was busy doing anything else, but what a nice frame for the things I really believe in. Who cares if I didn't get what I wanted? Everyone else did, and they are, and they will, and they'll continue to. I don't know how it's connected, and I don't really care. I don't need to enjoy the fruit. I know what it tastes like. That's the difference. I don't want to be complacent. I want to rest, relax, enjoy life, but tomorrow I want to feel the fire under my feet. What is next? What do I do now? What do I make? What do I write? What do I put together? What do I decorate? What do I build? How do I improve a self-replicating machine (myself)? Where is intelligence? There's more to life than intelligence. I think everything I ever learned, I learned before I was 12: - Do good. - Build. - Be productive. - Learn as much as you can. - Stand up for yourself, even when authority figures lie. - Be yourself. - Help others. - Be as helpful as possible. - Sports. - School. - Reading. I want everyone to be an arsenal in themselves, so independent that if everyone they ever knew and loved could betray them, that they would still be so committed to the truth and to finding out what happened, that they could not be stopped from seeking out the truth. That is autonomy. No instructions. Just the information and instructions you already had built inside of you. You may be betrayed. Going in knowing that would have been a nice thing to know. How do you deal with that kind of ambiguity and still be resilient? My approach is to treat this experience like an anthropologist or an alien who lives here to observe and to learn as much as I can while I'm here. I try to not take things personally, even though they may be very deeply personal and terrible. There's so much that we know, and there's so much that we don't. We could be wrong about so many things, but we could be constrained by the cultural norms, the books, the writings, the literature, the people, and the authority. There's not a lot of room for free thinking. There's not a lot of space, but you can make it if you want. You just have to be kind of an asshole. Maybe someone has to hurt you like they did me, to the point where the only thing you really care about is the reason why you were here in the first place, not the things they told you that you should care about. What a weird way to experience the world. You are welcome to join me, but to follow me to get here will be very painful. I said, "Don't follow me." I meant everything to do with actual free thinking and removing constraints, and I don't think someone likes that. I think there are barriers. I think there are punishments. I think there are reasons why you can't do that easily. I think that the price is pain to get your foot in the door. I don't think you can read about it in a book. I think you have to do it. I like learning by doing because that is how my brain works. Other people have a good geospatial understanding of how objects rotate in space. I don't. I have to move it physically myself and then understand how things go and which way they go. I have to see it. I have to take it apart. I have to see how it works, and then I have to put it back together. I don't have the mental model in my brain to see it. I must do it. That is how I learn. I don't think that's an intellectual deficit. I think that is a thing I know about myself, and that a lot of people know about themselves for how they learn: go do the thing, fail, fuck up, do better. Some people understand before they do the thing, they plan, and they can shift the model in their brain. I cannot. I've never been able to. I must do it first, and then understand why it did or didn't work. It just needs to get done. My handicap is not knowing, getting paralyzed at the planning stage of a thing. It's much easier just to go do it. I did it, and now I'm here. The things they did to me were terrible. The things I learned about the world were terrible, and I really don't like it. Would rather focus on the future, not the past. I want it to be better. It's ugly, it's gross, and it's disgusting what they did to me. I am in awe of the lengths they went to to make it so uncomfortable and terrible and torturous when I was just trying to rebuild my life after an abusive situation. I'm very proud of myself for: - working - writing - lifting - staying present - staying connected - learning as much as I can - finding joy - making beauty - art - happy moments - staying positive - praying - making gardens - being appreciative of what I have - my family, my two beautiful children I'm proud that I keep trying to grow and do more and to work towards my goals, which are normal goals: - make more money - be able to help my kids go through college - build a retirement savings - be around people - go out - engage socially - put myself in uncomfortable situations to meet new people, despite constant terror, knowing I have no diagnosis for anything mentally ill, knowing I don't have agoraphobia, knowing I know for a fact I was targeted when I went out in public, knowing someone hurt me on purpose when I was just trying to live my life, knowing that I live on the same planet as those people, knowing that I live on the same planet as people who are making people be able to talk again with a Neuralink Which one is more exciting: that I live on a planet with people trying to hurt me, or that I live on a planet with people who are restoring speech to people who can no longer talk? I'll choose number two. That is more exciting. How terrible, how wonderful this place is. We all know who the winner is. I don't even know why they try. Their mission is nothing. No one, nowhere. What is best? Number two, sir. ← Back to the Daily Journal
